title: Where the Sources Disagree: the first twenty rows
status: Verified rows only. Every quote was found on its page of the cited scan (or the cited web page), every printed page was checked against the leaf's own running head, every table was read from the page image and added up, and every number was matched to its quote. What could not be verified is in held_back and the review queue (docs/facts/README.md). No averaging, no silent choice.

rules.no_averaging: Values are never averaged, merged or reconciled. Every printed value stays visible with its source, edition and page.
rules.shown_first: Each row names which value is displayed first and writes the rule. The rule decides the order of display, never which value is true (pitch 2.5b).

status_ladder.adopted with reason: one value is shown first for a written reason, all others stay visible
status_ladder.open: no value is settled; the sources and what would settle it are shown
status_ladder.unresolvable: the sources cannot be reconciled because they describe different things or different moments

tiers.A1: public domain by date (published before 1931) or a US Government publication; quoted verbatim
tiers.B: facts only, attributed; a secondary compilation (here only US Government web pages of the National Park Service)
tiers.S: this project's own data, shown only to show where its numbers come from

rules.verification: figure-level methods: ocr_or_text (the number is in the text of the scan or page), image (read from the page image), second_scan (same book, another scan), ocr_corroborates_image (the OCR text of the page also holds the number); checksum = the figure sits inside a passing addition. See docs/facts/README.md.

values.authority: Official Records, list printed with Meade's report (August 1863)

values.what_is_counted: officers and enlisted men, ten rows (headquarters, eight corps, artillery reserve); killed 246 + 2,909; wounded 1,145 + 13,384; captured or missing 183 + 5,182

Fox's "final statement" of the Union loss, which he says has "lately been revised and corrected at the War Department"; he builds his table on "the recapitulation of losses, as published by Mr. Kirkley in 1886" and adds a column of killed or died of wounds; the wounded include the mortally wounded; his own name-by-name count of killed or died of wounds is a separate figure (5,291)
the p. 187 figures (his footnote d cites "43 W. R., 187"); he prints killed plus wounded (17,684) and missing separately and no grand total (23,049 is the sum)

a rounded estimate for the Union ("Estimated Casualties 51000 total (US 23000; CS 28000)")

values.authority: The site's own data: sum of the eight corps casualty fields
values.what_is_counted: the eight corps rows of the site (First, Second, Third, Fifth, Sixth, Eleventh, Twelfth, Cavalry), which leaves out the headquarters row (4) and the Artillery Reserve (242) of the p. 187 recapitulation
values.derivation: p. 187 total 23,049 - Artillery Reserve 242 - General headquarters 4

values.authority: The site's own data: sum of the per-period apportionment
values.what_is_counted: the site's "by engagement period" apportionment; this ledger could not trace the 89 men by which it exceeds 23,049

shown_first.rule: Official Records returns first (pitch 2.5b authority ranking for casualties); within the Official Records the revised statement the footnotes themselves point to (p. 187). A display order, not a claim that it is true.

rows.reason_for_difference: The Official Records print the Union total three times as 23,190 / 23,186 (the August 1863 list, Meade's report, Halleck's report) and once as 23,049 (the revised statement p. 187); each of the earlier places carries a note "But see revised statement, p. 187". Fox (1889) prints a third set, 22,990, which he calls the War Department's final revised statement and builds on Kirkley's 1886 recapitulation; he does not say how it differs from the p. 187 statement. Livermore (1900) uses the p. 187 figures. Jacobs (1864) rounds an estimate made in 1863. The site's 22,803 is the p. 187 total less headquarters (4) and the Artillery Reserve (242) (arithmetic). Missing includes captured men, so it is the least settled of the three counts.
rows.what_would_settle: The War Department compilation Fox cites (Kirkley, 1886) set beside the p. 187 statement, and a name-by-name roll count (Fox did one for the dead only).

review.what: Say whether Fox's 1886 "Kirkley" statement and the Official Records p. 187 statement are two compilations of the same nominal lists, and which the Park uses.

held_back.claim: Busey and Martin (2005): 23,055 (3,155 killed, 14,531 wounded, 5,369 captured or missing)
held_back.reason: facts-only tier B; the figure reaches this project only through Wikipedia and the site's facts.json ("p.125 as cited by Wikipedia; not opened"); the book was not opened and no accessible page was verified, so it is left out.
no source for this number was found; the only 22,8xx figures met were 22,803 (the site's corps sum) and 22,822 as an unrelated column total in Fox's table of battles.

rows.title: Confederate casualties at Gettysburg (killed, wounded, missing, total)
rows.question: How many Confederate soldiers were killed, wounded or missing at Gettysburg?

values.authority: Official Records, Return of Casualties in the Army of Northern Virginia (recapitulation, with Surg. Guild's statement)
values.what_is_counted: the compilation "at the battle of Gettysburg, July 1-3", which the editors call "approximative" and say is based on the figures of brigade, division and corps commanders where they differ from Surgeon Guild's detail

the returns (2,592 / 12,709 / 5,150) plus his own additions: 6,026 wounded and 275 missing "captured in excess of 770 reported", and 1,311 killed "to equal the average proportion of killed to 4.8 wounded"; no grand total is printed in the table (28,063 is the sum); his footnote 1, computing the number engaged on the returns of July 31, prints "losses at Gettysburg as above 28,070", 7 more than the sum, and does not explain the difference

values.authority: Jacobs, Notes on the Rebel Invasion (1864)
values.what_is_counted: a round estimate by a witness: "5,500 killed, 21,000 wounded, 9,000 prisoners, and 4,000 stragglers and deserters, or a total of about 40,000"; it counts stragglers and deserters, which the returns do not
a rounded estimate for the Confederates ("US 23000; CS 28000")

shown_first.rule: Official Records returns first (pitch 2.5b authority ranking for casualties), shown with the editors' own warning that it is approximative. A display order, not a claim that it is true.

rows.reason_for_difference: No Confederate total is settled. The Official Records return counts what commanders reported (and says many "missing" were killed or wounded, especially Pickett's division). Livermore adds to it: wounded and missing captured beyond the reported numbers (6,026 and 275) and 1,311 killed to match the average proportion of killed to wounded; the sum of his printed components, 28,063, equals the figure the pitch lists for the American Battlefield Trust (the Trust page was not fetched: link-out only), while his own footnote prints 28,070. Jacobs counts stragglers and deserters too. The NPS figure is a round estimate.
rows.what_would_settle: Name-by-name Confederate rolls (Krick, 2004, graded the brigade returns; not verified here), and the Union prisoner-of-war records the Official Records mention (see WSD-08).

review.what: Decide whether to show Livermore's printed components with his additions labelled as estimates, and whether to cite Krick and Busey and Martin once their pages are checked.
Facts-only attribution of Busey and Martin and Krick figures (pitch part 5).

held_back.claim: Krick (2004): 22,587; Stone Sentinels: 22,709; Busey and Martin (2005): 23,231 (4,708 / 12,693 / 5,830); American Battlefield Trust: 28,063; Livermore "27,823" as listed in the pitch
held_back.reason: none could be verified from an accessible source: Krick and Busey and Martin were not opened (Busey and Martin only as cited by Wikipedia), Stone Sentinels is a link-out source, the Trust bans scraping and was not fetched, and Livermore's printed figures give 28,063 (K+W 22,638 plus missing 5,425; his footnote prints 28,070), not 27,823.
